$comment: The scope object of spec §13j. Set by the field's experts, not by the agent and not by the owner. Versioned: a change here is a change to what the agent may work on.
principle: binding is a free-energy difference and structure determines it; every score is an approximation to one computable quantity

set_by.$comment: roles, never names — naming a person in a design document commits them to something they have not agreed to. `named` is filled when a panel exists.

in.boundary: which target, argued from biology supplied by the adjacent field
the receptor as an input to everything else
the cheap approximation, reported with its ceiling and baseline
the twin — where physics is computed rather than approximated
proposal, always downstream of an evaluation that does not leak
whether a proposal can be made
synthesise and assay — rung 6, and only with a body

out.question: whether a compound should be given to anyone
the claim that a binder is a drug

adjacent.relation: target biology — whether the thing bound is the thing that matters

claims_allowed: enrichment with its ceiling and property baseline on a series-disjoint split
prospective hit rate when measured, including when worse
claims_forbidden: any claim about a named individual
any statement that a result is clinically actionable without the endpoint role's sign-off
would_move_the_boundary: rung 6 becoming routine — the question turns into what to make next under an experimental budget, which is search under cost, not structure-determines-affinity
$watch_comment: if this rung stays blocked by a dependency the scope put out of bounds, the boundary is in the wrong place (§13j)
